note: Rewritten from the species-level description in Emerson 1960; the original is in English. For this species the source pack contains only the Comparisons paragraph (no Imago/Soldier subheadings precede it and the earlier body text is not included), so only a Diagnostic characters section is given, without caste subsections. Type locality: a Pygmy camp 4 km north of Camp Putnam on the Epulu River, Belgian Congo; holotype and paratypes comprise 6 soldiers and 1 worker; a further paratype colony from Yangambi comprises 5 soldiers and 2 workers. 'head width 1.10 mm' is kept verbatim.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier (a paratype soldier from Segboroué, Dahomey, compared with Mucrotermes osborni): body smaller, head width 1.10 mm; the elevation on the posterior part of the postmentum more pronounced; the concavity of the anterior margin of the labrum deeper; the sharp corners on either side of the labrum sharper, with deeper concavity of the lateral margins behind them; the elbow of each mandible situated relatively farther from the base; the concavity of the anterior margin of the pronotum shallower. Its soldier mandibles (especially at the base), the general shape of the head, the small elevation behind each antennal base, the inclination of the vertex, the position of the frontal gland opening and the pilosity, and the proportions of the maxillary palps, all indicate a close relationship with M. osborni; the worker mandibles are also close to those of M. osborni, only the apical tooth of each mandible being proportionally slightly larger. The species was originally placed in the genus Procubitermes.
